title: os migrate value rewrites skip a disabled module's extension columns without saying so
body:
domain:server#4 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CZMkHvuDeVYgTD73qF

Follow-up to card #30304 (PR #30362) and card #30377 (PR #30587), from the contract review of PR #30362, delta record 6654178714, should-fix 2. Recorded on #30377 as seat note 6654197160, item 2, and left out of PR #30587 because it is another package. Not blocking.

## Observed

The `os migrate` value-rewrite commands under `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/` (`blank-single-values`, `option-codes`, `text-scalars`, `value-shapes`) scope their rewrites by `engine.getObject(object)`, which is the served fold. While a module package is disabled, the fields its `objectExtensions` add are withheld from that fold (#30304), so a run skips those columns and leaves them for a later run after enable. The plan output does not say so. Read from the code, not measured with a run.

These commands read through `engine.find(fields: […])`, which refuses a withheld field by design (`INVALID_FIELD`), so moving them to the storage fold needs engine support and is not the small answer.

## Expected

The smallest honest answer: a run's plan output names each column it skipped because the package that adds it is disabled (object, field, package id), so the operator knows to re-run after enabling it. An alternative is for the run to warn or refuse while a module that extends a target object is disabled; the dev measures and picks one, and says why.

Pin it with one integration case per chosen behaviour: a module adds a field by extension, the module is disabled, the plan names the skipped column.

## Out of scope

Rewriting withheld columns while their package is disabled (needs a storage-fold read path in the engine).
